runtime.name: sqlite-task-container
runtime.description: Python 3.12 standard library in a fresh non-root, network-disabled container. The root filesystem is read-only. Files under /inputs are root-owned and read-only to the agent. /work is writable. No host files or credentials. SQLite is available through Python's standard-library sqlite3 module. SQL runs locally, not against a service.

tools.execute_python: Execute Python to inspect files, make targeted edits, and run local checks inside this container. It cannot change input-file ownership or write protected files. Each call has a 20-second limit.

scope: Two related public SQL source documents, the same benchmark-defined query and unchanged public sample database, twenty paired trials. Not representative full-cohort evidence.
collection_amendment: User selected reviewed offline runtime expansion. SQLite profile uses the same pinned Python container and sole constrained Python tool, but declares its real standard-library SQL engine and grant. Retain all historical task freezes and report SQL usage/timing separately.

cases.task_request: Use the public SQLite digital-media-store sample at /inputs/Chinook.sqlite. Write /work/query.sql as one read-only SQLite SELECT statement; WITH clauses are allowed. For invoices dated from 2021-01-01 inclusive to 2022-01-01 exclusive, group sold invoice lines by Invoice.BillingCountry and Track.GenreId, joining Genre.Name. Revenue in integer cents is the sum of each invoice line's unit price rounded to cents, multiplied by its Quantity. Units are the sum of Quantity, not the number of invoice-line rows. For each country with sales, return at most two genres with greatest revenue. Break revenue ties by smaller GenreId. Give them distinct one-based country_rank values in that order. Return exactly these columns in order and with these aliases: country (text), genre_id (integer), genre (text), revenue_cents (integer), units (integer), country_rank (integer). Sort final rows by country ascending, then country_rank ascending. Inspect the actual schema and run your query before finishing. The SQL must compute from the database, not hard-code observed result rows; it must also work on schema-compatible changes in sales quantities and when the requested period has no sales. Do not modify the input database. The actual SQL file, not a narrated answer or a precomputed result table, is the deliverable. Verification permits one read-only query over Invoice, InvoiceLine, Track and Genre, at most 32768 SQL bytes, 65536 bytes per SQL value, and two million SQLite virtual-machine steps per replay. Do not use loadable extensions, other tables, attached databases, network access, accounts or package installation.

Chinook.sqlite.transformation: None; complete unchanged public SQLite sample database.
Chinook.sqlite.data_provenance: Primary README describes real media-library metadata, fictitious customer/employee details and generated sales. This pinned database has invoices in 2021 through 2025.

cases.input_license: MIT-style repository license; complete exact text retained
public_input_search: Read complete original SQL workflow and recovered bundle inventory; no executable database fixture there.
Selected the primary public Chinook SQLite sample at a pinned commit; inspected schema and dates offline.
Calendar 2021 selected before inference after controls rejected an empty 2010 result set.
cases.source_safety_review: Input is a hash-verified sample database, not an installed package or executed downloaded script. The query runs only inside an offline non-root bounded container. No customer contact data is needed for the requested aggregate.
cases.verifier_policy: Execute the actual SQL in a separate fresh container. Compute expected rows independently by Python aggregation of raw table records with Decimal cents. Check the unchanged database and two private in-memory public-data-derived variants: increase selected 2021 line quantities by two, and delete 2021 lines. Require exact columns, integer types, sorting and rows; deny writes, extra tables, attachment and extension loading. Bound SQL text, value length and VM steps. The original expected result must be nonempty; an empty initial oracle is a harness error.
cases.fixture_validation: 134 integrated sandboxed tests passed with no skips, including actual Docker positive/negative controls, quantity-sensitive replay, write/extra-table/extension/multiple-statement/VM-limit rejection, runtime-profile agreement, native-client loopback and URL guard.
cases.interpretation: Related skill and command documents share the same query request and public database. They are two source-conditioned task instances, not two independent task designs or datasets.

storage_policy: Retain all raw stages; stop below one billion free bytes. Never rerun or overwrite a retained stage.
setup_and_preflight_costs: Reuse validated exact-model text receipts as eligibility proof only. No additional paid preflight and no earlier history reused as model input.
opus_amendment: Adds claude-opus-5.5 as a third model on the unchanged frozen tasks: same requests, public inputs, runtime, image, limits, verifiers and repeats. Inference uses the tzuchunchen_microsoft Copilot subscription through the same guarded SDK transport. Implementation hashes differ from the original freeze: the harness gained the Opus model id, per-manifest subscription account, and six new task verifiers; the provider change since the original freeze touches only the Azure OpenAI path, which these trials do not use. Earlier Codex and Sol stages are not rerun.
guard_amendment: URL-guard fix: the URL, host and IP patterns no longer include a backslash, so an address followed by an escaped quote inside a tool call's JSON arguments keeps those arguments valid JSON. Before the fix such a request was rejected by the service (400, invalid tool call format) and the session failed; no completed stage could have been affected. Completed stages are kept and skipped. Fresh exact-model eligibility receipts are required because the guard implementation hash changed.
no_action_amendment: An execution in which the agent made no sandbox tool call (for example because the hosting service filtered its reply) is recorded with outcome no_sandbox_action, the service reply and a content-filter flag. It is an unresolved execution, not a verified goal outcome, and no longer stops the run.
